item.title: Yemen’s collapsing healthcare forces the sick to seek alternative medicines
item.description: Patients in Yemen who cannot afford healthcare or access relevant treatment are turning to alternative medicine.

item.title: How Israel’s occupation fuels resistance
item.description: Israel is trapped in a cycle it created.

item.title: Trump’s former personal lawyer narrowly confirmed as US attorney general
item.description: US Senate confirms Todd Blanche in narrow vote despite concerns over independence of office.

item.title: Fiji rugby player dies in Japan of suspected heatstroke as high of 35C hit
item.description: Saimoni Vunilagi was hospitalised with symptoms of heatstroke after rugby team training on Monday, but died on Friday.

item.title: Mount Etna ash suspends arrivals at Italy’s Catania airport
item.description: Catania international airport services the eastern part of Sicily, one of Italy's most popular tourist destinations.

item.title: Newcastle say they “didn’t want to sell” Guimaraes, as Arsenal move looms
item.description: Bruno Guimaraes looks set to move to Premier League champions Arsenal, but Newcastle say they did not want to sell.

item.title: US announces $400m investment in Australian rare earth mine
item.description: Deal aims to secure scandium supply as China restricts exports for defence products.

item.title: Messi will decide when he retires, says Argentina FA chief
item.description: Retirement rumours surrounded Lionel Messi at last two World Cups, but Argentina FA chief says decision will be his.

item.title: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan, heads towards China
item.description: Five elderly people have suffered non-life-threatening injuries, with three falling due to the wind in Japan.

item.title: Afghanistan’s Rashid takes six wickets in ODI thrashing of Ireland
item.description: Rashid Khan forces collapse as Afghanistan beat Ireland by 92 runs in second game of five-match ODI series.

item.title: South Korea FA apologises over ‘sexual services’ allegations
item.description: Football association apologises over claims relating to qualifiers for World Cup 2014 and the London 2012 Olympic Games.

item.title: NBA star Brandon Clarke died from heroin, cocaine effects, examiner rules
item.description: Memphis Grizzlies ⁠forward Brandon Clarke's ⁠May 11 death ruled accidental, with effects of heroin and cocaine cited.

item.title: Hundreds camp on sweltering Rome street amid tussle over squatted building
item.description: After a fire broke out, the building was cleared in what activists say was a politically motivated move.

item.title: Bangladesh say Shakib will not play cricket again after Hasina event
item.description: Shakib Al Hasan says he will return home to face trial if safety assured, but Bangladesh rule out cricket comeback.

item.description: Palestinian Christians are facing violence and displacement across Gaza, Jerusalem and the occupied West Bank.

item.title: FIFA’s Infantino backed in Colombia where he attends president inauguration
item.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino gets South American football's backing while at Abelardo de la Espriella's inauguration.

item.title: Norway Football Federation calls for FIFA president to resign
item.description: Norway’s football federation has called on Gianni Infantino to resign.

item.title: Armenia puts Church leader on trial for allegedly being a Russian spy
item.description: Armenia’s head of the Apostolic Church and senior clergy could face jail time over allegations of spying for Russia.

item.title: ‘I’ve never been counted’: DR Congo’s first census in 42 years
item.description: For many Congolese, the census is about identity, recognition and finally being recorded by the state.

item.description: Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi had cancelled an earlier Saudi trip after deadly July 29 US-Saudi strikes on Iraq.

item.title: US Senate passes Russia sanctions that could hurt India and China
item.description: The US Senate approved its strongest move against Russia under Trump.

item.title: Submerged Indonesian village re-emerges as drought lowers water levels
item.description: Drone footage shows the remains of a submerged village re-emerging from Indonesia’s Karian Reservoir after a drought.

item.title: US courts clear way for deportations of South Sudan, Myanmar nationals
item.description: Rulings allow Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status for nationals of the two countries.

item.title: What could the Mecca defence pact mean for the US role in the Middle East?
item.description: Analysts say regional partners are seeking alternatives to supplement their security without discarding US support.
